text:
She always rewarded my visit

with the gold of an enchanting tale;

innocence lived in the little old woman

as sky water lives in a flower...


She adored children and blue;

she was always dressed in innocence,

and the clothes she kept in the trunk

smelled of basil and camphor...


How early-rising she and the doves were:

because the courtyard was covered in flowers,

it almost always dawned

beneath the trees, sweeping aromas...


And at night, in the lamplight,

she prayed with such deep devotion

that the moon, appearing at the balcony,

found her soul in the breviary.


One night among so many... alas, my friend

did not appear at the corridor again.

“She is ill,” they said: “a pain,

a weariness, a silence, a fatigue”...


The doctor came and began prescribing,

murmuring in a low voice: “She is very ill”...

And I learned the sad story: this was a wing,

tired of flying...


And did she leave? Like everything; four candles

filled the little room with sadness.

How that saintly whiteness of her head

was confused with the lilies!

translation.title: This Was a Wing
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the old woman’s devotional tenderness and the final wing metaphor, allowing “candor” to become the more idiomatic “innocence.”
